title: Acute Chest Pain / Suspected Coronary Syndrome
guidelines: ESC Guidelines on Non-ST Elevation ACS 2020
AHA/ACC Guideline for Evaluation of Chest Pain 2021
pathophysiology: Acute myocardial ischemia due to coronary plaque rupture or demand mismatch.

facts.onset: The chest pain started about 45 minutes ago while walking up the stairs. It has not gone away.
facts.symptoms: It feels like a heavy tight band squeezing the center of my chest, radiating to my left jaw and shoulder.
facts.history: I have hypertension and high cholesterol. I take atorvastatin and amlodipine. No drug allergies.
facts.risk: I feel nauseated, short of breath, and sweaty.
facts.exam: Patient is anxious, pale and diaphoretic. Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. Chest is clear bilaterally.

ecg.name: 12-lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
ecg.result: Sinus rhythm at 96 bpm; 2mm horizontal ST-segment depression in V4-V6 and inverted T-waves in aVL.
ecg.interpretation: Subendocardial ischemia in anterolateral leads consistent with acute Non-ST Elevation ACS.
ecg.why: Immediate priority (within 10 minutes of arrival) to differentiate STEMI from NSTE-ACS.

troponin.name: High-sensitivity Cardiac Troponin (hs-cTnI)
troponin.result: Initial sample: 185 ng/L (upper reference limit < 14 ng/L).
troponin.interpretation: Markedly elevated cardiac troponin indicating acute myocardial injury; serial testing indicated.
troponin.why: Confirm myocardial necrosis and stratify ischemic risk.

chest-xray.name: Portable Chest X-ray
chest-xray.result: Normal cardiac silhouette; no signs of pulmonary edema or widened mediastinum.
chest-xray.interpretation: Excludes pneumothorax and obvious aortic dissection signs; does not rule out ACS.
chest-xray.why: Evaluate alternative causes of acute chest pain if it does not delay reperfusion.

ct-head.name: CT head
ct-head.result: Not performed; no neurological deficit present.
ct-head.interpretation: Not indicated for acute chest pain.
ct-head.why: Unnecessary radiation and diversion from acute cardiac stabilization.

expected_actions: Continuous cardiac telemetry and venous access
Second antiplatelet (Ticagrelor or Clopidogrel) per local protocol
Sublingual or spray Nitroglycerin if SBP > 100 mmHg
Urgent cardiology consultation for early invasive strategy
critical_errors: Failing to obtain 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of presentation
Administering nitrates when patient is hypotensive or has taken PDE-5 inhibitors
Failing to initiate loading dose antiplatelet therapy for acute coronary syndrome
